note: research findings written to org/notes/retro-game-library-options.md: 12 live candidates checked against GitHub (stars, last push, latest release, license), grouped into four models - desktop launcher (Playnite MIT 10.63 2026-10-19; SimpleLauncher GPL-3 5.8.4 2026-10-20; ES-DE 3.5.0 2026-09-30 free on Win/mac/Linux with built-in scraper; OpenBoxGL AGPL-3 v1.19.1 2026-10-28), library server + clients (RomM AGPL-3 5.4.1 2026-10-22, 14,160 stars, imports LaunchBox metadata; Gaseous AGPL-3), import-into-Steam (steam-rom-manager GPL-3 2.5.44), build-our-own. options researched and written up; three questions handed to Brad - target device(s), desktop launcher vs self-hosted server with clients, and whether the metadata source matters / build-our-own is allowed. No install without his answer.
retro-game-library project registered + card-017 research landed (options note, 2 memory cells, qwen focus refreshed)

Brad answers the three scoping questions: incumbents are Pegasus and LaunchBox, target is WINDOWS, and RomM is a nogo because 'it struggles with PSP and Discs in general'. That settles device and model; PSP + multi-disc handling becomes the discriminator.

Brad rules: Windows desktop only, desktop app with no server, RomM excluded. Consequence: model B (RomM, Gaseous) and anything architecturally equivalent is off the table; project scoped to a Windows desktop frontend; PSP + multi-disc handling outranks artwork and UI polish.

Verification pass against the ruling, written into org/notes/retro-game-library-options.md (additive section). Checked against upstream source, not marketing copy: Playnite MIT 14,393 stars pushed 2026-10-19 - PPSSPP def Platforms sony_psp, ImageExtensions iso/cso/pbp/chd, StartupExecutable PPSSPPWindows64.exe; DuckStation def includes m3u/chd/pbp/cue; source/Playnite/Common/M3U.cs parses playlists incl RetroArch ':' and '|' suffixes; official docs state 'Playnite by default groups multi-disc games under one game entry' with split/merge on the right-click menu. LaunchBox survives in Playnite only as a metadata provider (Jeshibu/PlayniteExtensions manifests/Metadata_LaunchBox.yaml) - no LaunchBox library importer exists, so the library is re-scanned. ES-DE: multi-disc is manual (user-authored .m3u inside directories named like files, USERGUIDE 1316-1377), and psp is PPSSPP standalone single-disc only - out. SimpleLauncher GPL-3.0 266 stars pushed 2026-10-30: PSP searches cso/chd/iso/pbp/elf/prx with PPSSPPWindows64.exe, and ChdMountStrategy/DiscConverter give the deepest disc machinery of anything checked (CHD mount on 19 emulators, CHD->ISO, CHD->CUE/BIN, PBP->CUE/BIN) but there is no automatic m3u generation, no LaunchBox/Playnite import path, and metadata is RetroAchievements + image packs. OpenBoxGL AGPL-3.0 v1.19.1: PARITY.md marks multi-disc M3U generation done, but the app is a localhost server (handlers/, static/, 'server-computed capability contract') so it fails the no-server ruling, and emulator_defs/ppsspp-psp.yaml lists pbp/iso/cso with no chd.
